Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Situation2: They strictly follow a detailed schedule of daily prayers, chanting, and offerings, ensuring nothing is skipped.
Story: It was 3 a.m. when my phone buzzed, jolting me from a light sleep. I saw my friend’s name flashing on the screen, and when I answered, I was met with sobs. She could barely speak, but I understood enough—something terrible had happened in her family. As her friend, I knew I needed to listen, to be present, to offer comfort and let her pour out her pain. But as the minutes ticked by, my mind drifted to the small altar in my room. My daily prayers, the chanting, the offerings—they were all supposed to begin before dawn, at a precise time, as I had promised myself and my faith. Missing even a part of the ritual felt unthinkable, a break in the sacred rhythm I’d built my life around. I felt torn, guilt pressing in from both sides. My friend’s voice trembled through the phone, needing me, while the silent pull of my faith reminded me of my own spiritual commitments. My heart raced as I sat on the edge of my bed, phone in hand, caught between two worlds that both meant everything to me.
